sections.subtitle: The essentials in a few lines
content: This site sets no cookie and loads no resource from a third-party service (audience measurement, advertising, social networks, web fonts).

I measure the site's traffic with a tool I built myself. It never records your IP address, and the keys used to group the pages of a single visit are only used during the day, then deleted from the database.
The contact form stores nothing on the site: your message is sent to me by e-mail.

sections.subtitle: Audience measurement: why and on what basis
content: I measure the site's audience to know which pages are viewed, where visitors come from and which devices they use, to spot broken links and technical errors, and to improve the site.
These statistics are strictly reserved for me. They are neither sold nor passed on to third parties, and they are never combined with other data or with other sites.

Legal basis: my legitimate interest in knowing the audience of my site, with data limited to what is strictly necessary (Article 6(1)(f) of the GDPR). You can object at any time (see "Your choice: not being tracked").

sections.subtitle: What the audience tool records
content: For each page displayed: the page viewed, the language, the outcome of the request (page found, page moved, page not found or error), and the date and time.

To group the pages of a single visit: an internal visit number and, until midnight only, a visit key. It is a 32-character code computed from your IP address and your browser, using a secret that is never stored in the database and that changes every day. It does not allow your IP address to be recovered.
The type of your device (computer, mobile or tablet) and the family of your browser and operating system (for example Firefox or Windows).

The site you came from, reduced to its domain name (for example google.com, never the full address), and the campaign parameters utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign if they are present in the link you used.
For a page that does not exist (404 error): the address requested, without anything after a question mark, to spot broken links and automated intrusion attempts.
Finally, I tell human visitors apart from robots (search engines, link previews) and from my own test scripts, so that my statistics are not skewed.

sections.subtitle: What is never recorded
content: Your IP address (neither complete nor truncated), whether in the database or in any log of the tool.

The details of your browser for a human visitor, the full address of the page you came from, anything after the question mark of an address, your browser language, your country or city, a fingerprint of your browser (fonts, screen resolution, etc.) and any identifier shared between several sites.
The content of the contact form is never passed to the audience tool.

sections.subtitle: Anonymising visits
content: A visit groups the pages viewed with the same key on the same day, as long as less than 30 minutes separate two pages.
Until midnight (Paris time), the key is a pseudonym: it is only used to follow the course of a single visit during the day.

After midnight, the key is no longer used. It is deleted from the database at the first visit of the following day, or by a daily automatic task. Only an internal number then remains for the visit: nothing links it to a device or a person any more, so the data is anonymous.

sections.subtitle: Your choice: not being tracked
content: If your browser sends the "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control" signal, I honour it: no visit key and no browsing path is recorded for you.
A global daily counter is still incremented (page, language, outcome of the request). It contains no identifier and relates to no one in particular.
For any other objection, write to me at {dev_mail}.

sections.subtitle: Contact form
content: If you write to me through the form on the contact page, I collect your name, your e-mail address, your phone number (optional), the reason for your request and your message.

Purpose: replying to your request. Legal basis: my legitimate interest in replying to the messages sent to me and, if you propose a collaboration, the pre-contractual steps you request (Article 6(1)(b) and (f) of the GDPR).
The site does not store your message: it is sent to me by e-mail through my host's mail services and kept in my inbox. It is neither transferred, sold nor rented to third parties.

sections.subtitle: Cookies and trackers
content: This site sets no cookie on your device and loads no resource from a third-party service (audience measurement, advertising, social networks, web fonts). It therefore displays no cookie banner.
Links to other sites (LinkedIn, GitHub, etc.) are only links: those sites receive no data until you click, and are then governed by their own privacy policy.
If cookies were ever to be used, this page would be updated before they go live.

sections.subtitle: Hosting, recipients and security
content: The site and its database are hosted by {host_name}, which acts as a technical provider (processor). The site is served over an encrypted connection (HTTPS).

The web server's technical logs (IP address, date and time, requested address, browser) are kept by the host for the security and proper operation of the service. They are separate from my audience tool, and their retention period is set by the host under its own privacy policy.
The statistics are accessible only to me. Apart from my host, no data is passed on to anyone.

sections.subtitle: Retention periods
content: Visit key: no longer used after midnight, deleted from the database at the first visit of the following day or by a daily automatic task.
Visit details (pages viewed, device, origin): 13 months, then deleted.
Daily counters (number of pages viewed per day, page, language, outcome): kept without time limit, because they contain no identifier.
Addresses of pages not found and technical errors: 90 days.
Contact form messages: 12 months after the last exchange, unless a professional or contractual relationship is ongoing.
Backups: the host backs up the database over a rolling 7 days. During that time, a backup may contain the day's visit keys; they do not allow an IP address to be recovered.

sections.subtitle: Your rights
content: Depending on the case, you have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction and objection, as well as the right to portability of the data you gave me (GDPR, Articles 15 to 21, and the French Data Protection Act).
To exercise them, write to {dev_mail}. I reply within one month. If there is reasonable doubt about your identity, I may ask for proof of identity.

Audience statistics: once the visit keys are deleted, the remaining data is anonymous. It no longer allows you to be identified, so I can no longer find a visit in order to communicate, correct or delete it (Article 11 of the GDPR). To prevent any browsing path from being recorded about you, enable "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control" in your browser.
If, after contacting me, you consider that your rights are not being respected, you may lodge a complaint with the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).

sections.subtitle: Updates to this policy
content: This policy evolves with the site: it is updated before any new data collection (new cookies, new measurement feature).
Last updated: 31 October 2026.

Intro.title: About this site
texts: I am a developer: Java and Spring on one side, PHP, JavaScript, and ReactJS on the other, with a touch of Bash to automate repetitive tasks. I am looking for my first position in development, either remote or in my region.
I wrote this website myself in PHP using a custom MVC architecture. It is available in both French and English, and it can generate my A4 resume on the fly.
Design is not my specialty. I chose to keep it simple so that this site would finally exist rather than waiting indefinitely: perfection is the enemy of good.
This is just the beginning, and if you visit regularly, you will see it evolve.

messages.visiteurs: To you browsing here on the web: take your time to explore! Your feedback and advice are always welcome to help me improve this site.
messages.recruteurs: If you are here to evaluate my profile for a professional opportunity, the Career page gathers the essential details of my experience and lets you export or print my resume directly.

presentation.title: My Profile & Career
intro: I grew up in a family of market gardeners, working on local markets where I served my first customer at age 4. I enjoyed mathematics from an early age: Science Baccalaureate with a math major, intensive math prep, then university up to a Bachelor's degree (L3). That is where I discovered programming, along with relational databases and object-oriented programming.

After university, I worked for several years in commerce before launching my own business with a market stall. I needed a management tool, but none met my expectations. Rather than buying a software license, I preferred to build it myself.
I taught myself programming by searching for the language best suited for this project. I tried three:

languages.name: JAVA
languages.detail: Going further than what I had learned in college.

languages.name: C++
languages.detail: It allows creating executables, but it was not suitable for building the user interface.

languages.name: VBA (Visual Basic for Excel)
languages.detail: My final choice: interfaces were relatively easy to create and data storage was simple to handle, leaving more time for algorithms.

outro: The rest of my journey, driven by personal needs, led me to professionalize my software development skills.
I completed a training program to earn the professional certification for Web/Mobile Web Developer (AFORMAC in Bourges), where I acquired core web skills and methodology.
To continue advancing, I chose Java through a remote Bachelor's degree in Application Design & Software Development at Studi.

sitemap-manager.title: Sitemap Manager
sitemap-manager.shortDescription: Bash CLI utility to automate XML sitemap management and lastmod tag updates.
longDescription: A DevOps productivity tool designed to run from any project directory. It features an interactive loop menu, intelligent <loc> tag detection, and robust multi-OS AWK processing handling Windows/Linux line endings.
This project also incorporates automated terminal demo generation using the VHS tool to showcase its command-line workflow.

1.0.0: Project creation and setup of the initial structure.
Successful validation of sitemap update features by iteration over all declared pages.

jt-dev-flow.title: JT-Flow
jt-dev-flow.shortDescription: Bash CLI that creates a project structure from a profile and automates recurring tasks.
longDescription: Starting a project is always the same ritual: create the folder structure, copy the configuration files, run git init, and forget nothing along the way. JT-Flow is the command-line tool, written in Bash, that I am building to bring together the recurring tasks of my development cycle. Its init command creates the structure of a new project from a profile (java-api, java-app, php-web, php-api or react-app). These profiles are described in a configuration file rather than hard-coded in the script.

The architecture rests on three principles: a central router that reads the arguments or opens an interactive menu when information is missing; one lightweight script per action; and atomic functions, one function per task, so they stay reusable and maintainable. init is the most advanced command. The next ones (commit, release, merge, check, build, deploy) progress along with my projects. The goal: let the tool remember for me, so a typo no longer costs me an hour of debugging.
